SHORT_DESCRIPTION: INITIATIVES FOR LOCAL GOVERNANCE REFORM PROJECT
PROJECT_TITLE: Initiatives for Local Governance Reform Project
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The objective of the Initiatives for Local Governance Reform Project for Indonesia is to pilot support to district (labupaten) governments in improving transparency, accountability and public participatory practices and in undertaking reforms in financial management and procurement. The Borrower's changes include: (i) reducing the planned number of participating districts, (ii) completing the final round of reforms, simplify the reporting of reform requirements, and discontinue reform requirements that will be difficult to achieve within the next two years, (iii) providing additional incentives to performing districts, (iv) improving implementation support, and (v) reallocating the un-disbursed grant amounts to subprojects. This project paper also proposes to extend the closing date of the loan and credit by twenty-four months to September 2011, and the Department for International Development (DFID) grant by fifteen months to December 2010. These changes are expected to enable the project to focus on the existing participating districts and support them in achieving the development objectives in the next two years.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: JAVA-BALI POWER SECTOR RESTRUCTURING AND STRENGTHENING PROJECT
PROJECT_TITLE: Java-Bali Power Sector Restructuring and Strengthening Project
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Java-Bali Power Sector Restructuring and Strengthening Project for Indonesia aims to improve the performance of the power sector on Java-Bali by: (a) supporting the State power company (PLN) to implement its financial and corporate restructuring plan, and to strengthen key elements of the Java-Bali electricity supply system, and (b) assisting the State gas company (PGN) to prepare the groundwork for restructuring its gas transmission and distribution operations. There are five components to the project. 1) The Project will support PLN's initiatives to (a) achieve greater utilization of existing generation capacity on Java-Bali, (b) improve the security of supply to the cities of Cirebon and Surabaya, and (c) debottleneck local interconnections between bulk transmission and subtransmission. 2) The Project will support PLN's initiatives to (a) provide a level of security commensurate with the existing and potential PLN and PP geothermal generation capacity evacuated through the West Java 150kV subtransmission network near Bandung, (b) improve security of supply to Surabaya, and (c) relieve multiple localized overloading and voltage problems at subtransmission level. 3) The Project will support PLN to implement a pilot rollout of the company's Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) information system. 4) The Project will also support PLN's restructuring program-as well as its institutional strengthening initiatives-through technical assistance. 5) The Project will support PGN's restructuring and institutional strengthening initiatives, through technical assistance.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: PRIVATE PROVISION OF INFRASTRUCTURE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE LOAN
PROJECT_TITLE: Private Provision of Infrastructure Technical Assistance Loan
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The development objective of the Private Provision of Infrastructure Technical Assistance Project for Indonesia is to assist the Government in developing and implementing the policy and regulatory reforms and build the institutional and social foundations needed to enable, promote, and facilitate efficient and sustainable large-scale private investment in infrastructure. There are three main project components. The first component, Cross-sectoral technical assistance and advisory services, encompasses: Core support to the Secretariat for the Committee on Policy for the Acceleration of Infrastructure Development (KPPI Secretariat) and Planning and Investment Sub-committee, supplementary support to the KPPI Secretariat and Planning and Investment Sub-committee, and support for the establishment and initial operation of a central Public-Private Partnership (P3) unit. With the second component, the largest part of the project resources will be allocated to sector-specific activities aimed at establishing conditions conducive to sustainable private investment in infrastructure, and to developing specific opportunities for such investment. The project will focus primarily on the transport, telecommunications, and urban infrastructure sectors, and support activities involving: 1) legal and regulatory reform (drafting of sector laws and implementing regulations),2)design and establishment of regulatory institutions, 3) conduct of sector policy and strategy studies with a strong PPI focus and impact (including sector / sub-sector privatization strategy studies), 4) establishment of key sectoral nodes in the national P3 network, 5) preparation and tendering of pilot PPI projects, and 6) conduct and dissemination of lessons learned analyses for recent private infrastructure projects and privatization initiatives. The third component The project contributes to capacity building and training in areas relating to private participation in infrastructure.
